newsitem.title: USA: Congress says air carriers meet obstacles abroad.
newsitem.headline: Congress says air carriers meet obstacles abroad.

text.p: U.S. all-cargo airlines are meeting considerable problems at overseas airports, ranging from excessive red tape to denial to fly authorized routes, the U.S. General Accounting Office said on Friday.

The report by the GAO, Congress' investigative body, said many of the carriers said they had not reported their problems to the Transportation Department and some were unaware the department could help out.
It said the department should make known its ability to help and extend its current effort to collect data on the problems faced by all-cargo airlines operating overseas.

Senator Larry Pressler, a South Dakota Republican and who is chairman of the Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee, said it was "completely unacceptable" that the carriers reported problems at 81 overseas airports.
"U.S. cargo carriers must be able to compete fairly in any market. When U.S. cargo is disadvantaged, U.S. trade is hampered unfairly," he said."
Senator John McCain, an Arizona Republican, said: "It is imperative that we fix these problems" and that carriers be able to do business abroad in a fair and competitive manner.
Pressler and McCain requested the GAO study.
